title.narrative: improving primary health care and quality of life of persons living with & affected by hiv/aids

description.narrative:
Namu primary health care (PHC) is a Church link partner of CAFOD of Shendam diocese in northern Nigeria; the project is a continuation from the last PHC project which had participated in the piloting and development of HIV Quality of life tool by CAFOD in 2009. This was project support is a once off support for it to continue the work on HIV and AIDS thereby contributing to CAFOD current PPA. The need for this support came following the assessment of the QoL of the support group using the battery tool, it was discover that most of the participant’s reason for low batteries was as a result of lack of livelihood security and their inability to pay and obtain drugs for common opportunistic infections like malaria and respiratory tract infections.
The project aims at supporting and contributing to the delivery of CAFOD Programme Partnership Agreement (PPA 264) with DFID in the area of HIV and AIDS to achieve its outcome “CAFOD supports, influences and mobilises the Catholic Church to empower women and men in poor, vulnerable and marginalised communities to have greater access to and control over the resources and decisions that affect their lives.”
The specific contribution this project will make in achieve the set outcome will include: • Supporting 50 persons (35 women and 15 men) living with or affected by HIV and AIDS in the rural communities of Namu to access greater control over economic resources and health decisions that will improve their quality of life thereby contribute to the mainstream of their community development. This will be achieve by providing income generating revolving fund for the most vulnerable groups each year (50 women and 15 men), and learning opportunities to provide evidence for inclusion of additional new members.
• Outcome indicator: 70% percentage of women and men sampled, living with and affected by HIV who provide evidence of improved quality of life (PPA outcome indicator 3) and livelihood securities annually.
The output of this project is Namu PHC and its support group-Beacon+ of Hope members provide access to comprehensive (care, mitigation and prevention) services to reduce the impact of and vulnerability to HIV for 35 women, 15 men and 150 children yearly in Namu communities (PPA Output 3.). The output indicator is 35 women, 15 men and 150 children have increased access to a holistic range of care and mitigation services annually.
Input will include: Revolving fund transfer, revolving drugs for common opportunistic infections and a borehole for safe drinking water for clients, relatives and staff at the based clinic.
At the end of the project lifespan, 70% percentage of participants of the PHC and Beacon of Hope SG+ initiatives correctly identify ways of preventing HIV infection and reject major misconceptions about HIV transmission.
